###############################################################################
# Simple Graphs - GENERATED FILE. DO NOT EDIT BY HAND.
#
# Written by generate_faithculture_colors.py, which reads the authored colour
# of every vanilla faith and culture straight out of the CK3 install and emits
# it as script. Edit the generator, not this.
#
#   generated from : CK3 unknown
#   faiths         : 140
#   cultures       : 244
#   luminance cap  : 0.45
#
# WHY A GENERATED TABLE AND NOT A LOOKUP AT RUNTIME
# -------------------------------------------------
# Because there is no lookup at runtime. CK3 1.19 exposes no faith or culture
# colour to script or to GUI - no accessor on Faith, Religion, Culture,
# CulturePillar, CultureTemplate or CultureTemplateData returns a colour, and
# no effect or trigger reads one. The colours exist only in the game's own
# data files, so the only way to have them is to read those files before the
# game runs and ship the answer. The generator's header documents the cost.
#
# CONSUMER FILE. It names faiths and cultures on every line, which is exactly
# what a consumer file is for and exactly what rule 1 forbids an engine file
# from doing. The engine half of this feature is the palette in
# sg_engine_palette.txt, which names nothing.
#
# THE COLOURS ARE DARKENED relative to the authored values, by a single scale
# factor per colour that leaves hue and saturation untouched. The plot draws
# on vanilla's letter paper and a lot of map colours are too pale to see on
# it. See the generator's header.
#
# WHAT READS THESE VARIABLES
# --------------------------
#   sg_faithculture_color_r / _g / _b   0..1 per channel, per object.
#   gui/simple_graphs/sg_c_faithculture_window.gui turns them into the line's
#   colour with FixedPointToFloat, which is why they are stored as fractions
#   rather than 0..255 or packed into one number.
#
# An object with no row here keeps no colour from this file and is given a
# palette colour by sg_engine_assign_fallback_color_effect instead. That is
# every faith and culture created during a campaign, and every one added by
# another mod.
###############################################################################

# One line per object below, so the table stays readable as a table. The three
# variable names live here rather than at every call site.
sg_c_faithculture_set_color_effect = {
	set_variable = { name = sg_faithculture_color_r value = $R$ }
	set_variable = { name = sg_faithculture_color_g value = $G$ }
	set_variable = { name = sg_faithculture_color_b value = $B$ }
}

# Called ONCE per save, from sg_c_faithculture_snapshot_effect, guarded by the

# O(1) per object; asking each object "which key are you" from inside the
# collection loops would be O(objects x keys) and is why it is done this way
# round.
